name: ConstraintBench
description: Large language models are increasingly applied to operational decision-making where the underlying structure is constrained optimization. Existing benchmarks evaluate whether LLMs can formulate optimization problems as solver code, but leave open a complementary question. Can LLMs directly produce correct solutions to fully specified constrained optimization problems without access to a solver? We introduce ConstraintBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on direct constrained optimization across 10 operations research domains, with all ground-truth solutions verified by the Gurobi solver. Each task presents a natural-language scenario with entities, constraints, and an optimization objective; the model must return a structured solution that a deterministic verifier checks against every constraint and the solver-proven optimum. reputation: A very recent benchmark that is likely to gain attention in operations research and LLM reasoning circles, but is not yet broadly established.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark with deterministic verification; feasibility is the main bottleneck and the task is highly structured, so exact scores are sensitive to formatting and constraint adherence.
